transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because... I keep having these evenings where I end up buying a whole family-size takeout order. And then I'll usually add to it, like picking up bags of chips or bakery things from the store on the way home. And I just sit down and eat almost all of it myself before I even seem to register how much is actually gone. It's just gotten really out of hand.
After these episodes, do you deliberately try to compensate for what you ate?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, I feel terrible afterward, both physically and mentally, but... no, I don't try to make myself sick or go exercise for hours or anything. I usually just kind of sit there and deal with being overly full.
How often do these episodes happen?

Well, I actually keep a journal, and... when I look back through it, there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks it happens several times.
During these episodes, do you feel unable to control what or how much you are eating?

Yes, absolutely. Once I start, there is this awful switch that flips. I can literally be sitting there thinking, Taylor, put it away, but... my hands just keep opening containers anyway. It really feels like I am not the one in charge of what I'm doing.
During these episodes, do you eat noticeably faster than you normally would?

Yes, definitely. I eat so fast during those times that I barely even taste anything. I'll just be standing there at the dining room table with the microwave going and open boxes all around me, and... I'm basically swallowing one bite while I'm already reaching for the next.

Episodes occur several times per week over several months, with no compensatory behaviors, supporting binge-eating disorder.

Feels unable to control what or how much is being eaten.
Eats much more rapidly than usual.
Continues eating until physically overly full.
Experiences significant physical and mental distress afterward.
Denies self-induced vomiting, prolonged exercise, or other deliberate compensatory behaviors after episodes.
